sentences.text: JUDGMENT

The petitioner has filed this petition U/s 22 of the Workman Compensation Act 1923, claiming compensation amount of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest from the date of accident till date of realization, in respect of injuries sustained by the petitioner on 21.05.2022.
2.

The brief facts of the petitioner are summarized as under:
The applicant was a workman employed by the respondent No.1 as a "Driver" of the Tata Intra V 30 Goods Carrier bearing Reg.No.KA-41-D-2020, he was holding valid and effective driving license to drive the said vehicle.
On 21.05.2022 at about 5.30 a.m., as per the direction of the respondent No.1 the petitioner, during the course of his employment, was driving the Tata Intra V 30 Goods carrier bearing Reg.No.KA-41-D-2020 on NH-4 Bypass Road, along with one Ravi @ Ravikumar as a "Cleaner" and one Arun @ Arun Kumar traveling along with his goods, the petitioner's vehicle was reached at Aluru Cross, in front of Basavaraj Nursing College Cross road, Chitradurga, the vehicle of the petitioner came in contact to the rear portion of a lorry bearing Reg.No.TN- 29-AR-3602 thereby the petitioner and his cleaner and Arun Kumar sustained grievous injuries all over their respective bodies.
3. Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Hiriyur Government Hospital wherein fir aid treatment was given with suturing of wounds and then he was shifted to KIMS Hospital, Bengaluru wherein he was admitted as an in patient.

The x-ray report revealed that he had sustained abrasion over left forearm, lacerated wound over parital aspect of the skull of 6 cms, soft tissue contusion with hematoma in the right occipital region discharged with an advice for regular follow up treatment with complete bed rest.

4. The petitioner further pleaded that he has incurred Rs.1,00,000/- towards hospitalization,
conveyance, medical treatment, attendant, nursing care and other incidental expenses.
He is in need of future medical treatment and other incidental expenses.
5. Petitioner further submits that, he was hale and healthy and was aged about 42 years as on the date of accident.

He was working as Driver under the respondent No.1 and was earning Rs.25,000/-
per month.
He was maintaining his family out of said source of income and was a sole bread earner to his family.
Due to the accidental injuries he could not able to do any kind of work compared to his previous strategy.
The disability sustained in the accident has impacted on his earning capacity and as such himself and his family have suffered a lot by mentally, physically and financially.
6. The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the vehicle involved in the accident, are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, prays to award compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest from the date of accident till the realization.

2 Hence, prayed to allow the petition 7.
After registration of the petition.
Notices were issued against respondents.

In pursuance of service of notice the respondent No.1 and 2 have appeared through their counsels and the respondent No.1 has not filed the written statement, therefore the written statement of the respondent No.1 is taken as not filed.
The respondent No.2 has filed its written statements on behalf of respondent No.1 by denying the entire petition averments.
The insurance policy was in force as on the date of the accident and liability if any is subjected to terms and conditions of the policy.

Further denied the age of the petitioner, avocation, income, injuries sustained, treatment underwent by the petitioner,
disability certificate obtained by the petitioner, medical expenses, conveyance and nourishment of the said petitioner.
Further denied the other contents of the petition.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant.
Hence, prays to dismiss the petition.
8. In order to substantiate the claim petition, the petitioner is examined as PW.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.10.
Thereby the evidence of petitioner side was completed and case was posted for respondent evidence.
On 24.02.2025 leaned counsel for the respondent No.2 has submitted that there is no respondent evidence on behalf of respondents.
Hence, prayed to post the case for the arguments.
Prayer was taken on record.
As per the prayer of learned counsel for respondent No.2, the respondent evidence was taken as closed and the case was posted for arguments.
9. I have heard the arguments on both sides and perused the materials available on record.

10. Upon considering rival contentions raised by the parties, this tribunal has framed the following issues:
1. Whether the petitioners prove that he was "employee" under the respondent No.1?
2 . Whether the petitioners prove that he has sustained grievous injury on 21.05.2022 at about 5.30 a.m., due to the actionable negligent during the course of employment under the respondent No.1?
3. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so how much and from whom?
4.
What order ?
11. My findings on the above issues are as under.
Issue No.1 :

In the affirmative,
 Issue No.2 : In the affirmative,
 Issue No.3 : Partly in the affirmative,
 Issue No.4 : As per the final orders for  the following:-
 REASONS ISSUE NO.1 and 2 :

sentences.text: These issues are taken up together for discussion to avoid repetition of facts as these issues are inter connected to each other.
The burden of proving these issues lies upon the petitioner.
13. To substantiate the petition averments, petitioner examined himself as PW.1 by reiterating the contents of petition and got marked 10 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.10.
Ex . P.1 FIR which reveals that one Muniraj.N has lodged complaint on 21.05.2022.
Upon the complaint, the police have registered FIR for the offence punishable under section 279 and 337 of IPC.

Ex.P.3 is the spot mahazar along with sketch, Ex.P.5 is the IMV report, Ex.P6 is the charge sheet which clearly shows that, on the alleged date, time and place of the accident has occurred and in the said accident the offender vehicle is involved in the occurrence of the same.
14. The petitioner was subjected to cross- examination by learned counsel for respondent No.1.
During the course of cross-examination of PW.1 nothing was elicited from the mouth of PW.1, so as to disbelieve his version.

15. Therefore, it is apparent on the face of records that, the respondents have admitted the occurrence of accident and death of deceased has caused due to the lack of safety measures and have failed to provide the same during the course of employment.
Hence, I answer issue No.1 and 2 are in the Affirmative.

ISSUE No.3:
16.
The petitioner has claimed compensation for a sum of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest from the date of accident till its realization.
On the basis of the materials on record, it is necessary to examine claim of petitioner in appropriate manner.
In support of the case petitioner has come up with various materials.
As such it is necessary to examined the materials on record in the parameter of pecuniary and non-pecuniary character.
17. Ex.P.8 is the wound certificate reveals that the petitioner has sustained injuries in the alleged accident.
But the petitioner, to prove that he sustained injuries, has not examined the treated doctor or any other doctor and disability certificate is also not produced.
Without the evidence of doctor it is not possible to believe that, the petitioner has sustained any grievous injuries.
18. In the petition the petitioner has stated that, he has spent Rs.1,00,000/- towards medical and other expenses.
Further Ex.P.7 is the medical bill reveals that the petitioner has paid an amount of Rs.5,351/- and Ex.P.8 is the medical prescription.

Looking to the injuries sustained and treatment taken by the petitioner and medical expenses, it is just and proper to award Global compensation of Rs.1,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum.
19. Admittedly, the respondent No.1 and 2 are the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, the respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer is bound to indemnify the respondent No.1.

sentences.text: Hence, respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation to petitioner with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
Accordingly, I answer this issue partly in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.4:-
20.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.1,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,. from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
The respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.
Considering the quantum of amount awarded to petitioner, it is ordered to release the entire amount in his favour.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/-.
Draw the award accordingly.
